Augustinian Biography of Robert F. Prevost, O.S.A.
--------------------------------------------------

Robert Francis Prevost was born on September 14, 1955, in Chicago, Illinois, to Louis M. and Mildred A. Prevost.

He studied for four years at St. Augustine High School Seminary in Holland, Michigan, where he earned his diploma in 1973. He continued in the Pre-Novitiate formation program at Villanova University in Villanova, Pennsylvania, earning a B.S. in Mathematics in 1977.

Robert was received into the Augustinian Novitiate on September 1, 1977. He professed temporary vows in the Order of St. Augustine on September 2, 1978. He completed theological studies at Catholic Theological Union in Chicago and earned a Master’s of Divinity Degree in 1981. He professed solemn vows on August 29, 1981, and was ordained a priest on June 19, 1982. From 1981 to 1985, he studied Canon Law at the Pontifical University of St. Thomas Aquinas (Angelicum) in Rome. He earned a Licentiate in 1984 and a Doctorate in 1987.

Father Prevost was named Chancellor of the Diocese of Chulucanas, Peru, in 1985. He returned to the United States in 1986 and served as Vocations Director for the Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel until 1988. He also was temporary Director of the Province Mission Office during this time.

In 1988, Father Prevost returned to Trujillo, Peru, to initiate the first common formation house between the Vicariates of Chulucanas, Iquitos, and Apurimac. In this community, in service to the pre-novices and the professed, he occupied the posts of Prior (1988-1992), Formation Director (1988-1999), Master of Professed (1993-1998), and parish priest of the Parish of Saint Mary of Monserrat. In the Archdiocese of Trujillo, he served as the Prefect of Studies at the Archdiocesan Seminary of San Carlos and San Marcelo, and he also taught Canon Law there. During this time, he also served as Judge of the Regional Ecclesiastical Tribunal and as a member of the College of Consultors in Trujillo.

He was elected Prior Provincial of the Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel in 1998 and returned to the United States to begin this role in 1999.

At the Ordinary General Chapter of 2001, Father Prevost was elected Prior General of the worldwide Augustinian Order. He was elected to a second term at the Ordinary General Chapter of 2007 and served until his term ended in September 2013.

Following his time as Prior General, Father Prevost returned to the Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel and served in several roles: Director of Formation at St. Augustine Friary, Vicar Provincial, First Counselor, Board Member of Villanova University, and Board Member of Catholic Theological Union.

On November 4, 2014, it was announced that Pope Francis had appointed Father Prevost as Apostolic Administrator of the Diocese of Chiclayo, Peru, and Titular Bishop of Sufar. He was installed as Apostolic Administrator of Chiclayo on November 7, 2014, and was ordained Titular Bishop of Sufar on December 12, 2014. He was installed as Bishop of Chiclayo on September 26, 2015.

Within the Episcopal Conference of Peru, he served on the permanent council from 2018-2020. He was elected in 2019 as President for the Commission on Education and Culture. He was also a member of the leadership of Caritas Peru.

On July 13, 2019, Bishop Prevost was appointed to the Vatican’s Congregation for the Clergy. From April 15, 2020, until May 26, 2021, he served as Apostolic Administrator of the Diocese of Callao, Peru. On November 21, 2020, he was appointed to the Vatican’s Congregation for Bishops.

On January 30, 2023, Pope Francis appointed Bishop Prevost as Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops (formerly Congregation of Bishops) with the title Archbishop-Bishop Emeritus of Chiclayo. He was also appointed the President of the Pontifical Commission of Latin America. He began both of these roles on April 12, 2023.

It was announced on July 9, 2023, that Pope Francis would elevate Archbishop Prevost to be a Cardinal at the Vatican consistory on Sept. 30, 2023. At the ceremony, he gave a speech on behalf of the other cardinals-elect. He continues to serve as Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops and as President of the Pontifical Commission of Latin America. He is also a member of several other Dicasteries.

On February 6, 2025, he was elevated from Cardinal-Deacon to Cardinal-Bishop within the College of Cardinals. He was assigned the title of the Suburbicarian Church of Albano.

On May 8, 2025, he was elected Pope and chose the name Pope Leo XIV.

11.title: Pope Leo XIV, American Catholicism and international politics
11.content:
US Vice President and American Catholic J.D. Vance sat down for an [interview](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/05/21/opinion/jd-vance-pope-trump-immigration.html) with _New York Times_ columnist Ross Douthat at the US Embassy to the Holy See in Rome last May.

**_Douthat:_**_So we’re here in Rome, the day after the papal inauguration, and you just met with Pope Leo XIV, the first American pope._

**_Vance:_**_I did._

**_Douthat:_**_So what did you talk about?_

**_Vance:_**_Well, I want to be respectful of the private conversation we had._

_Generally, we talked about issues the Vatican cares a lot about. Obviously, they care about the migration issue. They care a lot about world peace. They care a lot about what’s happening in Russia and Ukraine. They care a lot about what’s happening with Gaza and Israel. It was a very productive conversation. I mean, amazing to me. As you know, I was one of the last world leaders to meet with Pope Francis on Easter Sunday, before he passed away. I’m actually wearing the tie that he gave me, which is very cool._

Vance is as good an entry point as any for a reflection on the current state of Catholics and politics in the United States and what we might expect will become of Pope Leo’s relationship with them. While he is the most important Catholic in elected office in the US today (more on that in a minute), Vance is certainly not representative of the whole of American Catholicism. But who could be?

![Image 1: Pope Francis is seated at a large wooden desk and is speaking with a man in a suit](https://aspeniaonline.it/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/vance-pope.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV meets with U.S. Vice President JD Vance in the library of the Apostolic Palace at the Vatican May 19, 2025.

American Catholicism has always been distinguished by a teeming diversity that has evolved alongside social, cultural and political change in the country. Catholics who fill the pews on any given Sunday, in mixed and not-so-mixed parishes across cities, exurbs and rural counties, could be recent migrants from Venezuela, Brazil, the Philippines, Vietnam or the DRC; or they might be third or fourth or fifth generation combinations of Irish, Italian, Cuban, Polish or Mexican Americans; or Americans who have forgotten their distant origins altogether. Some worship as charismatics; some mix Pentecostalism in with their devotions; some are tied to the Latin mass; or Eucharistic Adoration; others still like their folk music; many liturgies are prayed in Spanish; and lots more are boring and plain with pretty bad music and lots of donuts.

Within American politics, the socio-economic diversity that this global mix represents makes the Catholic vote look a lot like the US population as a whole. As opposed to the more or less consolidated voting blocs of Evangelicals, Mormons, Jews, or non-Religious, Catholics are split between the two parties, and they have consistently voted with slim to modest majorities for the Presidential winner for decades, including for Reagan, Clinton, G.W. Bush, Obama, Trump, Biden (according to some [polls](https://news.gallup.com/opinion/polling-matters/324410/religious-group-voting-2020-election.aspx)) and Trump again. The public policy interests of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops do not fully correspond, therefore, to either the Republican or Democratic party platform: they have been consistently against abortion _and_ welcoming of migrants.

At the same time, important shifts in American Catholicism are underway and they have been especially noticeable at the level of elite Catholic politics and intellectual debates, both of which have influenced some of the ideological positions animating the ascendant Republican right. Vance, in particular, has close ties to post-liberal Catholic intellectual circles, including Patrick Deneen of the University of Notre Dame, and Sohrab Ahmari of _Compact Magazine_. As the title of Deneen’s bestselling book makes clear, the post-Liberals view the project of liberalism as having failed today, and they see that failure as the result of the long run decline of liberal nations’ Christian moral foundations, upon which liberal societies simultaneously rely (especially for social solidarity), but which they also destroy from within.

This diagnosis helps explain the culture war mentality which has gripped the Trump administration, perhaps most evidently seen in their attack on institutions of higher education like Harvard University. Like liberalism as a whole, many post-Liberals perceive Universities to be bad faith actors who have instrumentalized academic freedom and principles of neutrality to marginalize Christian moral values from the public sphere, greatly damaging the fiber of American society in the process. Obama-era policies which sought to [enforce progressive social changes](https://www.settimananews.it/informazione-internazionale/us-elections-biden-and-catholic-politics/) and judicial victories, in part, helped to feed some of these perceptions, which would then successively grow in response to the “peak woke politics” of the covid-era.

##### Read also: [**The Holy See’s paramount role: moral leadership in times of social unravelling**](https://aspeniaonline.it/the-holy-sees-paramount-role-moral-leadership-in-times-of-social-unravelling/)

The post-liberal logic extends to the sphere of international politics and institutions, which are viewed with similar suspicion and ill-intent. In response, American post-Liberals have supported more openly Christian and nationalist politics which are clear about protecting the identity of the United States as a Christian nation, as well as the moral foundations which spring from that. Vance’s hostility to European free speech laws, security policies and trade can be read in this light: not only is Europe seen as an ungrateful freeloader – see Vance on “[I just hate bailing out Europe again,](https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/archive/2025/03/trump-administration-accidentally-texted-me-its-war-plans/682151/)” – like Harvard, it is viewed as a cipher for (a failed and hostile) liberal culture and politics. The Trump administration’s attacks on the liberal international system, therefore, arise in part from these ideological and cultural positions.

So what does all of this mean for Pope Leo XIV, the first American (i.e. US-born) Pope?

One of the most important things about Pope Leo is that he stands outside of the American and global culture wars. He also appears to stand largely outside of the US Catholic Bishops Conference, which has been deeply affected by political and social polarization in the United States. Leo became a parish priest in Peru in the 1980s, long before the post-liberal turn, when the US Catholic hierarchy was more optimistic about its dealings with liberalism, and he has spent his career listening to the hopes and fears of the global Catholic Church.

As Pope, Leo will be required to engage the US Church, and perhaps directly with Vice-President Vance, not primarily because he is an American Pope, but because the fate of American Catholicism is important for the future of global Catholicism and the future of the international order within which it operates. As indicated above, the order we have inherited from the late 20 th century – the liberal international system – is in a dangerous phase of transition, rocked by violent crises, ideological challenges and the apparent withdrawal of its primary architect, the United States.

A new model of international order is not yet apparent and transnational religious traditions are being looked to for orientation as a result. It is quite possible that the College of Cardinals placed a bet on Robert Francis Prevost, as an insider-outsider, as an institutionalist, as someone devoted to the concerns of global Catholicism, waging that he was well placed to help manage this moment of transition. It is a risky bet, one that is vulnerable to getting sucked into the pathologies of US politics, but it also has important potential payoffs, especially if Leo were to succeed in mobilizing American Catholics, both those in the pews and those in politics, for the one public policy he has placed at the center of his papacy from day one, namely, international peace.

**A John Paul II-Francis synthesis?**

One way that this could play out would be for Pope Leo to adopt a kind of Pope John Paul II-Pope Francis synthesis in his governing style and concerns.

From the perspective of global politics, Pope John Paul II embodied the moral triumph of the liberal international order as it emerged at the end of the Cold War. In part, his public advocacy sprang from the Catholic Church’s new positions which it forged with liberal modernity in the aftermath of World War II – especially on freedom and dignity and rights. Those positions led to a wave of Catholic activism in support of democratization and human rights in authoritarian contexts across the globe, including by a young Fr. Bob Prevost in Peru in the 1980s.

In some ways, particularly in its beginnings, the papacy of Pope Francis took these foundational norms for granted and assumed that international cooperation could be constructed on a shared vision of universal dignity, freedom and rights. Francis’ public concerns, on the environment, migration, interreligious dialogue or sustainable development, might be understood in this optic as second generation rights which became clearer and pressing in part because first generation rights seemed more or less settled and secure. Francis largely avoided theological reflection on the political foundations of that order as a result and focused instead on the social and moral need for solidarity (or [fraternity](https://www.vatican.va/content/francesco/it/encyclicals/documents/papa-francesco_20201003_enciclica-fratelli-tutti.html)) to make that system work for those on the peripheries.

##### Read also: **[Assessing the Geopolitics of Pope Francis](https://aspeniaonline.it/assessing-the-geopolitics-of-pope-francis/)**

From Vance’s quote above, it looks like Pope Leo spoke his mind to him on at least two issues which put him in direct continuity with Pope Francis, namely, international peace and migration. Leo will now have to figure out how to pursue those policies in a fragmented and contested global system. To work towards international cooperation on peace, on the environment, or on development, however, he may need to go back to the fundamentals, the basic package of dignity, freedom, democracy and rights, in order to institutionally steer and ground the Church’s international diplomacy and civil-society-level public actions. Such a back-to-the-basics approach could help clarify, motivate and bring coherence to the Church’s positions, for example, in both Gaza and Ukraine, as well as in the United States.

A John Paul II – Francis synthesis might provide a simple directional for Leo’s pontificate, namely: to pursue Francis’ global social agenda with renewed commitment to the norms guiding John Paul II’s international politics. In their own ways, both popes continued the theological and political reforms begun at Vatican II which opened the Catholic Church towards modernity in a way that Leo XIV’s namesake positively anticipates (as Leo XIII marked the dawn of Catholic social thinking and political modernity). Combining the two, therefore, could also likely suit the personality, experience and intuitions of Leo himself, whose young religious life and politics came to age in John Paul II’s pontificate.

It is worth remembering that Pope John Paul II was deeply beloved by the American Catholic Church, who felt his loving gaze upon them and who were called by him to international responsibilities and solidarities. As such, a John Paul II-Francis synthesis might also help Pope Leo’s appeal to VP Vance, and to the rest of the teemingly diverse American Catholic Church, to build local and global solidarity with those on the margins – as Prevost had previously done on behalf of Pope Francis – but also to reimagine global and democratic politics which reflect those solidarities better.

Pope Leo XIV’s motto, _in Illo uno unum_, rhymes in interesting ways with that ancient American ideal, _e pluribus unum_. Both are lofty and bold as political agendas. They also indicate the deep fractures besetting our international system today. We can only hope for Leo’s success as he pursues these unities in the name of peace.

10.title: 2025 conclave
10.content:
| Papal conclave May 2025 |
| --- |
| Dates and location |
| 7–8 May 2025 [Sistine Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistine_Chapel "Sistine Chapel"), [Apostolic Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Palace "Apostolic Palace"), [Vatican City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_City "Vatican City") |
| Key officials |
| Dean | [Giovanni Battista Re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Battista_Re "Giovanni Battista Re") |
| Sub-dean | [Leonardo Sandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Sandri "Leonardo Sandri") |
| Camerlengo | [Kevin Joseph Farrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Joseph_Farrell "Kevin Joseph Farrell") |
| Protopriest | [Michael Michai Kitbunchu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Michai_Kitbunchu "Michael Michai Kitbunchu") |
| Protodeacon | [Dominique Mamberti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Mamberti "Dominique Mamberti") |
| Secretary | [Ilson de Jesus Montanari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilson_de_Jesus_Montanari "Ilson de Jesus Montanari") |
| Election |
| Electors | 133 ([list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_electors_in_the_2025_conclave "Cardinal electors in the 2025 conclave")) |
| Candidates | See _[papabili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025\_conclave#Papabili)_ |
| Ballots | 4 |
| Elected pope |
| **[Robert Francis Prevost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV")** Name taken: **Leo XIV** |
| [![Image 1: Portrait of Archbishop Edgar Peña Parra wearing a pectoral cross and biretta looking at the camera with a smile on his face](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Pope_Leo_XIV_3_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Pope_Leo_XIV_3_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_3_(cropped).jpg) |
| ←[2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_conclave "2013 conclave") |

A [conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave "Conclave") was held on 7 and 8 May 2025 to elect a new [pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope "Pope") to succeed [Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis"), who had died on 21 April 2025. Of the 135 eligible [cardinal electors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_electors_in_the_2025_conclave "Cardinal electors in the 2025 conclave"), all but two attended. On the fourth ballot, the conclave elected Cardinal [Robert Francis Prevost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Francis_Prevost "Robert Francis Prevost"), the prefect of the [Dicastery for Bishops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Bishops "Dicastery for Bishops") and president of the [Pontifical Commission for Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_Latin_America "Pontifical Commission for Latin America"). After accepting his election, he [took the name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_name "Papal name")_Leo XIV_.

Papal election process
----------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Papal election process")]

The papal election process proper began sixteen days after the 21 April 2025 [death of Pope Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_funeral_of_Pope_Francis "Death and funeral of Pope Francis"). As in the [2013 conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_conclave "2013 conclave"), the [dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_of_the_College_of_Cardinals "Dean of the College of Cardinals") and vice-dean of the [College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals") were both over 80 and ineligible to participate. In 2025, these were [Giovanni Battista Re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Battista_Re "Giovanni Battista Re") and [Leonardo Sandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Sandri "Leonardo Sandri"), respectively. The most senior elector under 80, [Pietro Parolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Parolin "Pietro Parolin"), who was also Cardinal Secretary of State, presided over the 2025 conclave.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-1)

### Timing and procedures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Timing and procedures")]

According to [John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Paul_II "John Paul II")'s 1996 apostolic constitution _[Universi Dominici gregis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universi\_Dominici\_gregis "Universi Dominici gregis")_, as amended by [Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_XVI "Benedict XVI")'s 2013 apostolic letter _[Normas nonnullas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normas\_nonnullas "Normas nonnullas")_,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Bonanata_2025-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Caputo_2025-3) the [cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_(Catholic_Church) "Cardinal (Catholic Church)") had at least 15 days after the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") became vacant to convene. The cardinals had the discretion to start the conclave earlier or up to 20 days after the pope's [cathedra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedra "Cathedra") became vacant.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Bonanata_2025-2) On 28 April 2025, two days after Francis's funeral,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-4) the fifth general congregation of the cardinals set the conclave to begin on 7 May 2025.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zengarini-2025-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-6)

Cardinals aged 80 years or older on the day before the papacy fell vacant were ineligible to participate. At the time of Francis' death, there were 252 cardinals, of whom 135 were under 80 and thus were not precluded from participation and voting in the conclave.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-BBC-2025-7) Of these potential electors, 108 (80%) had been elevated to the College of Cardinals by Francis;[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-9) the cardinal electors were also global and more diverse than in any prior conclave — they came from more than 70 countries and in many cases were the first cardinal ever appointed from their country.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-10)

Since the 1975 promulgation of _[Romano Pontifici eligendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romano\_Pontifici\_eligendo "Romano Pontifici eligendo")_ by [Pope Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_VI "Pope Paul VI") and the 1996 apostolic constitution _[Universi Dominici gregis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universi\_Dominici\_gregis "Universi Dominici gregis")_ by [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II"), the maximum number of cardinal electors had been 'set' at 120.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Hodge-2025-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-12) At 133, the 2025 conclave was the largest ever,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-13) and the first conclave where this purported limit was exceeded on the day the papacy became vacant.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-120+-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Campisi_&_Gussie_2025-14) Any cardinal under the age of 80 not having renounced or lost his voting rights has the right to vote in a conclave under [Catholic canon law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_canon_law "Catholic canon law"). A pope appointing more than 120 eligible cardinal electors effectively renders the 1975 limit inapplicable,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Jeyaretnam-2025-16) as popes John Paul II, Benedict XVI, and Francis all did;[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Campisi_&_Gussie_2025-14) although in the cases of John Paul II and Benedict XVI, the 120 limit at the conclave was not surpassed.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Hodge-2025-11)

On 30 April 2025, the general congregation of cardinals confirmed that all cardinal electors present for the conclave beginning on 7 May could vote.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-17) Ineligible cardinals could nevertheless attend the general congregations and participate in discussions preceding the conclave.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-18) Although the conclave cardinals have the authority to elect any Catholic male who has been [baptized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptized "Baptized"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Caputo_2025-3) the last time a non-cardinal was elected was in the [1378 conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1378_conclave "1378 conclave").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-20)

After saying he would try to participate in the conclave,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-21) Cardinal [Giovanni Angelo Becciu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Angelo_Becciu "Giovanni Angelo Becciu"), who had "renounced his rights as a cardinal" in 2020 due to his involvement in a financial scandal,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Pinto-2025-22) stated that he would abide by Francis's wish that he refrain from participating.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-23) Health problems prevented cardinals [Antonio Cañizares Llovera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Ca%C3%B1izares_Llovera "Antonio Cañizares Llovera") of Spain and [John Njue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Njue "John Njue") of Kenya from participating in the conclave,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-24) reducing the number of potential electors to 133; accordingly, the two-thirds supermajority required to elect the new pope was determined at 89 votes. This was the largest number of cardinal electors ever to participate and vote in a conclave.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-25)

Francis's hospitalization in February and March 2025 fueled speculation about an impending conclave.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-26) Due to the major international expansion of the membership of the College of Cardinals under Francis to 252, with over 140 non-European [cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_(Catholic_Church) "Cardinal (Catholic Church)") appointed during his pontificate, some observers had suggested a non-European pope was likely.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-BBC-2025-7)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Jeyaretnam-2025-16) The 2025 conclave was initially planned to have 135 electors from 71 countries; the 2013 and 2005 conclaves had had 115 electors from 48 and 52 countries respectively. Some of the participating cardinals did not speak Italian, the [working language of the Roman Curia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_language_of_the_Roman_Curia "Working language of the Roman Curia").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Dom%C3%ADnguez-2025-27)

Following the Italian saying "[fat pope, thin pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fat_pope,_thin_pope "Fat pope, thin pope")", some commentators predicted that Francis's successor would be more conservative.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Jeyaretnam-2025-16)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-28) There were also concerns of interference, which had been prohibited in 1996 by John Paul II,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-29) and a potential hostile takeover by [ultraconservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultraconservative "Ultraconservative") politicians and Catholics.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-31) As of the third and fourth general congregations, there was reportedly a desire among the cardinals for a ten-year pope, someone in his late seventies with experience in the [Roman Curia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Curia "Roman Curia") who would be more focused on internal affairs.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-32)

Some commentators posited a younger pope as more likely;[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-33) others felt that cardinals like [Pierbattista Pizzaballa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierbattista_Pizzaballa "Pierbattista Pizzaballa") and [Robert Prevost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Prevost "Robert Prevost") were too young.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-BBC-2025-7)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-35) Many cardinals expressed hope for a short conclave, as in 2005 and 2013.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-36) Given the complexities and heterogeneity of this conclave,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-37) compared to the two-day one that elected Francis in 2013,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_News_Agency-38) Cardinal [Rainer Woelki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainer_Woelki "Rainer Woelki") expected the 2025 conclave to take longer;[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_News_Agency-38) the Cardinals [Louis Raphaël I Sako](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Rapha%C3%ABl_I_Sako "Louis Raphaël I Sako") and [Gregorio Rosa Chávez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorio_Rosa_Ch%C3%A1vez "Gregorio Rosa Chávez") anticipated a short conclave of two or three days,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-40) with the latter remarking "maximum three days".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-41)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-42)

[Vaticanologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaticanologist "Vaticanologist") consider (by a variety of criteria) some cardinals to be more likely to become pope than others– these are the _[papabili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papabili "Papabili")_ (the plural for _papabile_), Italian for "pope-able".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-43) In practice, however, conclaves have not always chosen one of the _papabili_. Prior to his election in the [October 1978 conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_1978_conclave "October 1978 conclave"), [John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Paul_II "John Paul II") was not considered to be in the running.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-44) This is reflected in the saying "He who enters the conclave as pope, leaves it as a cardinal,"[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-45) although the frontrunner is often elected pope, as was the case in [1939](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1939_conclave "1939 conclave") ([Pius XII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pius_XII "Pius XII")), [1963](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_conclave "1963 conclave") ([Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_VI "Paul VI")), and [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_conclave "2005 conclave") ([Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_XVI "Benedict XVI")).[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-46)[Anna Rowlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Rowlands "Anna Rowlands"), a Vaticanologist, suggested that attempts to predict the conclave's outcome were based in "pure speculation".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-47) Media worldwide released _papabili_ analyses on the day of Pope Francis's death.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-48)_Papabili_ mentioned in the media included [Anders Arborelius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anders_Arborelius "Anders Arborelius"), [Jean-Marc Aveline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Marc_Aveline "Jean-Marc Aveline"), [Fridolin Ambongo Besungu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fridolin_Ambongo_Besungu "Fridolin Ambongo Besungu"), [Timothy Dolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Dolan "Timothy Dolan"), [Wim Eijk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wim_Eijk "Wim Eijk"), [Péter Erdő](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C3%A9ter_Erd%C5%91 "Péter Erdő"), [Fernando Filoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Filoni "Fernando Filoni"), [William Goh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Goh "William Goh"), [Mario Grech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Grech "Mario Grech"), [Claudio Gugerotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Gugerotti "Claudio Gugerotti"), [Pietro Parolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Parolin "Pietro Parolin"), [Pierbattista Pizzaballa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierbattista_Pizzaballa "Pierbattista Pizzaballa"), [Malcolm Ranjith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_Ranjith "Malcolm Ranjith"), [Robert Sarah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Sarah "Robert Sarah"), [Marcello Semeraro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcello_Semeraro "Marcello Semeraro"), [Luis Antonio Tagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Antonio_Tagle "Luis Antonio Tagle"), [José Tolentino de Mendonça](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Tolentino_de_Mendon%C3%A7a "José Tolentino de Mendonça"), [Peter Turkson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Turkson "Peter Turkson"), [Lazarus You Heung-sik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazarus_You_Heung-sik "Lazarus You Heung-sik"), and [Matteo Zuppi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matteo_Zuppi "Matteo Zuppi").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-49)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Maddox-2025-50)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Agenzia_ANSA-2025-51)

[Robert Prevost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Prevost "Robert Prevost"), the eventual elected pope, was speculated on as _papabile_,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-52)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-53)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-54) being the prefect of the powerful [Dicastery for Bishops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Bishops "Dicastery for Bishops"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-55) an ally of Francis, and a possible compromise candidate;[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Rich-2025-56)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-57) however, he was considered a [dark horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_horse "Dark horse"),[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Maddox-2025-50) and his American nationality had been regarded as a potential stumbling block to his candidacy, reflecting unease about enhancing the United States's geopolitical power after the re-election of [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") in 2024.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Maddox-2025-50)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-58) Supporters argued that Prevost represented a "dignified middle of the road".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Rich-2025-56) Some commentators felt that a non-European pope was likely due to the increased numbers of African and Asian cardinals,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-BBC-2025-7)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Jeyaretnam-2025-16) which reportedly ultimately collapsed Parolin's candidacy.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Agenzia_ANSA-2025-51) By contrast, others felt that a European pope was a more likely outcome,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Maddox-2025-50) remaining convinced that the reasons for why an American pope had never been elected before, namely the American status as [superpower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superpower "Superpower"),[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-60) still applied. James Bretzke, a theology professor at [John Carroll University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carroll_University "John Carroll University") in Ohio, told _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA\_Today "USA Today")_ that the best possible candidate was one who could be a diplomat, adding: "America's image in the world simply is too powerful– and to be blunt, ugly."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Maddox-2025-50)

Before the announcement of the conclave itself, prediction markets were using market mechanisms to calculate who might be in the running and their putative rankings.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-61)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-63) Upon Francis's death, the top five contenders were Tagle, Parolin, Zuppi, Ambongo, and Erdő, all of whom had been cited by Vatican journalists and analysts as _papabili_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-64) On the day of Prevost's election, the leading candidates on [Polymarket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymarket "Polymarket") were Parolin at 37%, Tagle at 26%, Pizzaballa at 10%, Erdő at 8%, Turkson at 7%, Sarah at 4%, and Zuppi at 3%. Parolin's odds to be named as the new pope jumped to nearly 70% after the white smoke was revealed, with many suspecting that the relatively short four-round conclave indicated a consensus candidate had been chosen.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-65)

Fantapapa ([Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language") for 'Fantasy Pope') was a [fantasy league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_league "Fantasy league") based in Italy for betting nominal sums on [papal conclaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave "Conclave"). Established by anti-gambling advocates Pietro Pace and Mauro Vanetti specifically for the 2025 conclave,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-66) the sole payout was "eternal glory". By 5 May 2025, it had 75,000 players in Italy, where no licensed platform offers gambling on conclaves.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-67) Fantapapa players chose from and ranked eleven cardinals; other aspects of the conclave, such as the papal name, language, number of rounds, and the day on which white smoke appears, were also available to bet on. Players gained points in accordance to their team members being "mentioned prominently" in domestic and international media coverage. The fantasy league was open to punters internationally and also offered mini-lessons in the Italian language.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-68)

Pre-conclave events
-------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Pre-conclave events")]

### Logistical preparations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Logistical preparations")]

[![Image 2: A large, light-colored building with many windows sits on a city street](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae.jpg/250px-Domus_Sanctae_Marthae.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Domus_Sanctae_Marthae.jpg)

Cardinals participating in the conclave stayed at [Domus Sanctae Marthae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae "Domus Sanctae Marthae").

Following the death of Pope Francis, preparations began at Domus Sanctae Marthae for housing the cardinal electors. These included setting up barriers or opaque film at the windows to prevent outside contact and the construction of spaces for the celebration of the [Sacrament of Penance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrament_of_Penance "Sacrament of Penance"), private prayer, and meals.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Il_Mattino-2025-69)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Garay-2025-70)[Signal jammers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_jammers "Signal jammers") were used to isolate the electors from [Bluetooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluetooth "Bluetooth"), [Wi-Fi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wi-Fi "Wi-Fi"), and [mobile networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_network "Mobile network").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Garay-2025-70)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-71)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Cybernews-2025-72) Because the building has only 129 bedrooms, it was necessary to provide accommodations for the 133 electors and support personnel,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-74)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-75) who stayed at Santa Marta Vecchia, next door to the main dormitory.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-76)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_Review-2025-77)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-78)

In the Sistine Chapel, preparations included the addition of tables and chairs in the manner of [choir stalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choir_stalls "Choir stalls") and the covering of windows; the ballot-burning stove and the chimney, which together serve to signal the results to the outside world, were installed,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-79)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-The_Washington_Post-2025a-80) as was a temporary wooden floor which served to protect the marble inlay, provide a more level surface, and hide electronic signal jammers.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-The_Washington_Post-2025a-80)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-NPR-81) Both the Domus Sanctae Marthae and the Sistine Chapel were thoroughly inspected in advance of the conclave for any unauthorized devices.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Garay-2025-70) On 2 May, [Vatican firefighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corps_of_Firefighters_of_the_Vatican_City_State "Corps of Firefighters of the Vatican City State") installed the chimney for the Sistine Chapel.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-82)

The [Vatican Gendarmerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Gendarmerie "Vatican Gendarmerie"), under the leadership of [Gianluca Gauzzi Broccoletti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluca_Gauzzi_Broccoletti "Gianluca Gauzzi Broccoletti"), faced many [counter-espionage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter-espionage "Counter-espionage") challenges in protecting conclave integrity.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Dom%C3%ADnguez-2025-27)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Garay-2025-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Cybernews-2025-72) The [Corps of Gendarmerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corps_of_Gendarmerie_of_Vatican_City "Corps of Gendarmerie of Vatican City") used the 650 [security cameras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_cameras "Security cameras") in the Vatican, [encrypted messaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encrypted_messaging "Encrypted messaging"), and [endpoint detection and response](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endpoint_detection_and_response "Endpoint detection and response") to secure the conclave.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Cybernews-2025-72) Meals for the 2025 conclave featured simple dishes [typical of Lazio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_Lazio "Cuisine of Lazio") and [Abruzzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_Abruzzo "Cuisine of Abruzzo"), the [regions of Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_Italy "Regions of Italy") nearest the Vatican.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-83)

### General congregations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: General congregations")]

[![Image 3: St. Peter's Basilica map view, showing its location next to the Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Square](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Conclave_Map.svg/250px-Conclave_Map.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Conclave_Map.svg)

Map of the major venues of the conclave

According to Catholic canon law, general congregations are daily meetings of all cardinals regardless of elector status and begin before all of the elector cardinals arrive in Rome. The initial meetings are focused on the logistics of the papal funeral and the conclave, including physical preparations at the Domus Sanctae Marthae (as a dormitory) and the Sistine Chapel (as a polling place). Later ones, typically the eighth and following, shift to discussions about the needs of the church and the world, and the issues facing the Roman Curia.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-84)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-85)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-86) These later general congregations are guided by the reflections given by two "distinguished and morally authoritative" clerics who are selected by the cardinals.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-87) The cardinals are also given the opportunity to make formal remarks regarding the issues facing the church.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-88) All of these speeches and discussions are termed _interventi_ ("interventions") in Italian.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-89) The general congregations meet in the New Synod Hall, on the first floor of the vestibule of the much larger [Paul VI Audience Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_VI_Audience_Hall "Paul VI Audience Hall").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-90)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-91) For the 2025 conclave, the general congregations met every day from 22 April following Francis's death until 6 May,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-92) excluding 26–27 April,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-93) 1 May,[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-94) and 4 May,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-95) with the beginning of the conclave proper on 7 May.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-96)

General congregations allow the cardinals to meet on their own initiative, thereby getting to know each other and exercise their [spiritual discernment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discernment_in_Christianity "Discernment in Christianity"); many had never met,[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-97) as Francis did not hold meetings of cardinals before his [papal consistories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_consistory "Papal consistory").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-98)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-120+-15) Furthermore, the cardinals have full access to global media and their diverse analyses and criteria for identifying the _papabile_.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-99) Before leaving for Rome on 24 April, Cardinal [Pablo Virgilio David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Virgilio_David "Pablo Virgilio David") stressed that a conclave is not a political campaign but a [religious retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retreat_(spiritual) "Retreat (spiritual)"). He also emphasized that it is a duty of the [College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals") to discern each other via prayer, [personal letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_letter "Personal letter"), and even research on a website with biographical and other information set up for that purpose,[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-100) and that it is not a matter of [candidates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candidate "Candidate").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-101) Both the formal and informal discussions are expected to be very substantive in preparation for, and in the hope of, a speedy conclave.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-102)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-103) The discussions held at cardinals' own initiative—_pratiche_, or exercises—are the most frank and candid.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-104) By canon law, the congregations are bound to the same secrecy as the conclave.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-105)

On 22 April, members of the [papal staff and household](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_staff_and_household "Papal staff and household") were asked to vacate their rooms at the Domus Sanctae Marthae following the death of Pope Francis in his suite on the second floor to allow for conclave preparations in that building to begin.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Il_Mattino-2025-69) The same day, the first of twelve general congregations were held. At the first congregation, the approximately sixty cardinals present listened to [Kevin Farrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Farrell "Kevin Farrell"), the [Cardinal Camerlengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Camerlengo "Cardinal Camerlengo"), read the [will and testament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_and_testament "Will and testament") of Francis. The canonization of [Carlo Acutis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Acutis "Carlo Acutis"), originally scheduled to take place in Rome on 27 April, was suspended, and the cardinals confirmed the date for the papal funeral. This meeting also dealt with the logistics of the funeral.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-106)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-107) The attending cardinals took the oath of secrecy concerning their meetings.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-108) Despite the fact that general congregations are closed to non-cardinals, Sister [Simona Brambilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simona_Brambilla "Simona Brambilla"), a [religious sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_sister "Religious sister") and the first woman to head a Vatican department (the [Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Institutes_of_Consecrated_Life_and_Societies_of_Apostolic_Life "Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life")), was accidentally sent a standard email inviting her to participate.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-109) On 23 April, the [Vatican Museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Museums "Vatican Museums") announced the closure of the Sistine Chapel beginning on 28 April, due to the needs of the conclave.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-110)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-111) At the second congregation, the program for the _novendiales_, or nine-day period of mourning for the deceased pope, was approved.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-112) Cardinal [Norberto Rivera Carrera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norberto_Rivera_Carrera "Norberto Rivera Carrera") stated to the press that these discussions had been mostly procedural in nature, as many cardinals from around the world were still traveling.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-113)

[![Image 4: Catholics in black cassocks and red hats sit in a tiered conference room](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Assembl%C3%A9e_du_Synode_des_%C3%A9v%C3%AAques_sur_la_famille_en_2014.jpg/250px-Assembl%C3%A9e_du_Synode_des_%C3%A9v%C3%AAques_sur_la_famille_en_2014.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Assembl%C3%A9e_du_Synode_des_%C3%A9v%C3%AAques_sur_la_famille_en_2014.jpg)

Cardinals and bishops in the [New Synod Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Synod_Hall "New Synod Hall") (pictured in 2014), one of the venues for the general congregations

The third congregation on 24 April, with 113 cardinals present, saw the appointment of the two conclave preachers, [Donato Ogliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donato_Ogliari "Donato Ogliari") and Cardinal [Raniero Cantalamessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raniero_Cantalamessa "Raniero Cantalamessa").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-114)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-115) At the fourth general congregation on 25 April, the 149 cardinals in attendance listened to a presentation on Francis's funeral rite.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-116) By this time nearly 70 formal speeches, or "interventions", had been given.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-117) There was also discussion concerning the status of Giovanni Angelo Becciu as a cardinal elector among the participants, which continued in the following congregations until his 29 April acceptance of his non-elector status.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Pinto-2025-22)

The fifth general congregation on 28 April determined that the conclave would begin on 7 May, sixteen days following Francis's death.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zengarini-2025-5)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-118) This meeting also discussed the [clerical sexual abuse crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_sexual_abuse_cases "Catholic Church sexual abuse cases"), challenges in [evangelization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelization "Evangelization"), and [ecumenism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecumenism "Ecumenism"). Twenty cardinals delivered interventions.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-119) Conservative cardinals, such as [Gerhard Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Ludwig_M%C3%BCller "Gerhard Ludwig Müller") and [Francis Arinze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Arinze "Francis Arinze") (not an elector), were particularly vocal during this session.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-White-2025-120)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-121) The next day, at the sixth congregation on 29 April, the start time for the conclave was set at 4:30 p.m., and [Cardinal Re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Re "Cardinal Re") was chosen as the celebrant for the opening Mass for the conclave.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Vatican_News-2025-122)[Donato Ogliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donato_Ogliari "Donato Ogliari") gave his scheduled reflection to the 183 cardinals present, 124 of them being electors, emphasizing the theme of synodality from the Francis papacy.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-White-2025-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Vatican_News-2025-122)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-123)

The seventh congregation on 30 April featured a discussion of the Vatican's financial issues by the 180 cardinals present, 124 of whom were electors.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-124)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-125)[Rainer Woelki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainer_Woelki "Rainer Woelki") stated that the meetings thus far had been "fraternal and cordial... a very concentrated, calm, factual working atmosphere".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_News_Agency-38)[Beniamino Stella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beniamino_Stella "Beniamino Stella"), not an elector, made a very strongly-worded critique of Francis's decision to allow [lay persons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_laity "Catholic laity") to exercise powers of church governance formerly reserved to [clergy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_orders_in_the_Catholic_Church "Holy orders in the Catholic Church"). This surprised many cardinals, as Stella was viewed as one of Francis's most trusted advisors and a prominent supporter of Parolin.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-126)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-127)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-128)

The general congregation did not meet on 1 May, the feast of [Saint Joseph the Worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph_the_Worker "Saint Joseph the Worker"), a [public holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_holiday "Public holiday") for the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") and an ecclesiastical counterpart to the secular [International Workers' Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Workers%27_Day "International Workers' Day") observed on the same day.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-129) The _[National Catholic Reporter's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Catholic\_Reporter "National Catholic Reporter")_ Rome bureau reported that Prevost was "emerging as a serious frontrunner".[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-130) At the ninth congregation on 2 May, 177 cardinals were present, of whom 127 were electors. Twenty-six cardinals spoke. Among the subjects discussed were: communion (_[koinonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koinonia "Koinonia")_) within the church and fraternity in and with the world; the hope of some that the next pope would be 'prophetic'; and the [2025 Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Jubilee "2025 Jubilee").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-131) The tenth and eleventh congregations were both held on 5 May and discussed a wide range of church topics.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-132)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-133) On 6 May, the twelfth and final congregation of the College of Cardinals took place.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Brockhaus-2025-134) This congregation witnessed the ceremonial destruction of Francis' symbols of office: his [fisherman's ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisherman%27s_ring "Fisherman's ring") and [lead seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulla_(seal) "Bulla (seal)").[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Brockhaus-2025-134)

[![Image 5: A Vatican Swiss Guard is seen in full uniform knocking on a wooden door](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/A_Swiss_Guard_Unlocks_the_Door_Outside_of_the_Sistine_Chapel_for_Secretary_Kerry_%2811948661293%29.jpg/250px-A_Swiss_Guard_Unlocks_the_Door_Outside_of_the_Sistine_Chapel_for_Secretary_Kerry_%2811948661293%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_Swiss_Guard_Unlocks_the_Door_Outside_of_the_Sistine_Chapel_for_Secretary_Kerry_(11948661293).jpg)

The doors of the Sistine Chapel (pictured in 2014) were shut at 5:46 p.m. on 7 May.

On 7 May, the conclave began. It was preceded by Cardinal [Giovanni Battista Re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Battista_Re "Giovanni Battista Re"), the dean of the College of Cardinals, celebrating the Mass _pro eligendo Pontifice_ (lit.'for the election of the Pontiff') in [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica") at 10 am [CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time") (08:00 UTC).[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-135) All support staff, such as [sacristans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacristan "Sacristan"), medical staff, elevator operators, and the director of security services for the Vatican, along with officers and officials of the conclave, had taken their solemn oath of secrecy on 5 May.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_Review-2025-77)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-136) At 4:30 pm, the conclave officially began with a prayer service in the [Pauline Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cappella_Paolina "Cappella Paolina"), at the end of which the electors entered the Sistine Chapel in procession. Once there, the hymn _[Veni Creator Spiritus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veni\_Creator\_Spiritus "Veni Creator Spiritus")_ ("Come, Creator Spirit") was sung and the 133 cardinal electors then swore themselves to secrecy.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-NPR-81)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Vatican_News-2025-122)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Brennan-2025-137) Each cardinal elector in order of seniority placed his hands on a [Book of the Gospels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_the_Gospels "Book of the Gospels") and made the affirmation aloud in Latin:[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Povoledo-2025-138)

> > _Et ego_ [prænomen] _Cardinalis_ [nomen] _spondeo, voveo ac iuro. Sic me Deus adiuvet et haec Sancta Dei Evangelia, quae manu mea tango.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025\_conclave#cite\_note-139)_
> 
> 
> 
> Translation:
> 
> 
> > And I, [forename] Cardinal [surname], do so promise, pledge, and swear. So help me God and these Holy Gospels, which I touch with my hand.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Povoledo-2025-138)

While making the oath, several cardinals used the Latin forms of their names.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Krupa-2025-140)[Diego Ravelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Ravelli "Diego Ravelli"), the [papal master of ceremonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_master_of_ceremonies "Papal master of ceremonies"), then called out the words _[Extra omnes](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/extra\_omnes "wikt:extra omnes")_, a command for everyone who is not a cardinal elector or an official of the conclave to leave the chamber.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Krupa-2025-140) He then shut the entrance to the Sistine Chapel at 5:46 p.m.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Brennan-2025-137)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Krupa-2025-140) Cardinal [Raniero Cantalamessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raniero_Cantalamessa "Raniero Cantalamessa"), the longtime Capuchin preacher of the pontifical household, then offered a reflection to the cardinals behind the closed doors.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-141) Reportedly, the remarks lasted for over an hour, delaying the start of the first ballot (and, consequently, the smoke reporting out its results); at one point, Cardinal [Parolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Parolin "Pietro Parolin") asked the assembled cardinal electors if they wanted to postpone the first vote until the next morning — (they did not).[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-:0-142)

Given the conclave had begun in the afternoon, only a single ballot was held on this first day.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zengarini-2025-5) According to some reports, Parolin, the frontrunner, received more than 40 votes on the first ballot, while the rest of the field was considerably split.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Agenzia_ANSA-2025-51)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Meichtry,_Stancati,_Lovett_&_Walker_2025-143)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zurlo-2025-144) According to other reports, [Prevost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV") was the most voted candidate in the first ballot, slightly above Parolin, with [Péter Erdő](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C3%A9ter_Erd%C5%91 "Péter Erdő"), one of the main conservative candidates, in third place.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-145)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-146) The first day of the conclave ended at 9:00 p.m., after black smoke emerged from the chimney of the Sistine Chapel, signifying that the vote taken had not resulted in the election of a new pope.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Krupa-2025-140)[Vatican Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Media "Vatican Media") reported that up to 45,000 people had gathered in [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square") to await the smoke.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-147)

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:White_Smoke_Papal_Conclave_2025.webm "Play video")Duration: 11 seconds.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:White_Smoke_Papal_Conclave_2025.webm)

White smoke billowing from the Sistine Chapel chimney. Faithful onlookers rejoiced, shouting "_[Habemus papam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habemus\_papam "Habemus papam")_!" ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language "Latin language") for 'We have a pope') and "_Viva il papa_!" ([Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language") for 'Long live the pope') in [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square").

[![Image 6: Pope Francis waves to the crowd from the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica, Vatican City](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg/250px-Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV on the loggia of St. Peter's Basilica following his election

The second day of the conclave began with two ballots, concluding at approximately 10:30 a.m. and 11:45 a.m., respectively.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-148) Black smoke appeared at 11:51 a.m., again signifying that no pope had been elected. Smoke is not produced after each ballot, but rather only at the end of each session (ballot cards from two unsuccessful votes in a morning session or two votes in an afternoon session are usually burned together once each pair of votes has been completed).[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-149)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-150)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-151) According to several reports, during this morning session of day 2, Cardinal Parolin received 40 to 50 votes but failed to pick up support from African and Asian cardinals, some of whom started to support Prevost. Pope Francis's strongest supporters were divided between Cardinals [Jean-Marc Aveline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Marc_Aveline "Jean-Marc Aveline") (France) and [Mario Grech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Grech "Mario Grech") (Malta), while Asian cardinals were splitting their votes between the two Filipino Cardinals [Luis Antonio Tagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Antonio_Tagle "Luis Antonio Tagle") and [Pablo Virgilio David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Virgilio_David "Pablo Virgilio David"). Cardinal Prevost enjoyed broad support from South American and [Anglosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglosphere "Anglosphere") cardinals, thanks also to the strong support of [Timothy Dolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Dolan "Timothy Dolan"), who supposedly functioned as something of a [kingmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingmaker "Kingmaker").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Agenzia_ANSA-2025-51)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zurlo-2025-144)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Giusti-2025-152) The cardinals then returned to the Domus Sanctae Marthae for lunch,[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Quotidiano_Nazionale-2025-153) where the breadth of support for Prevost became clearer.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Meichtry,_Stancati,_Lovett_&_Walker_2025-143)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-:0-142) Cardinals later told the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") that the result was becoming clear by the third ballot, as the votes were moving toward Prevost.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-AP122025-154) Pope Leo XIV later stated that after the third ballot, "I resigned myself to the fact when I saw how things were going and I said 'This could be a reality.'"[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-AP122025-154) By the end of the morning session, there were 15,000 people in St. Peter's Square and 5,000 people at the basilica of [Santa Maria Maggiore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_Maggiore "Santa Maria Maggiore"). More were expected during the afternoon session, since in the two most recent conclaves a new pope had been elected on either the fourth or fifth ballot.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-155)

After the lunch recess, the cardinals returned to the Sistine Chapel for the next and fourth round of voting.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Quotidiano_Nazionale-2025-153) The cardinals' support coalesced around Prevost, who received more than the two-thirds majority of 89 required: he reportedly received more than 100 votes on the fourth (and final) ballot.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Meichtry,_Stancati,_Lovett_&_Walker_2025-143)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Giusti-2025-152)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-156)

Parolin, as the most senior cardinal in the conclave, asked Prevost if he accepted his election as Supreme Pontiff, and by what [papal name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_name "Papal name") he would be known. Having quietly accepted his election, Prevost announced to the cardinals his chosen papal name _Leo_,[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Meichtry,_Stancati,_Lovett_&_Walker_2025-143) chosen at least in part to honor [Pope Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-157)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-158) Following the pope's acceptance of his election, the cardinals applauded, and he embraced them. He then exited the Sistine Chapel to the Room of Tears to be robed in the garments prepared there for the new pope.

After the fourth round of voting, white smoke appeared at 6:07 p.m., followed by the ringing of the bells of St. Peter's Basilica, confirming and signifying the election of a new pope.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-159)[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-160)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-161) Soon afterwards, the [Swiss Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Guard "Swiss Guard") and members of the [Italian Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Armed_Forces "Italian Armed Forces"), along with the bands of the [Gendarmerie Corps of Vatican City State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gendarmerie_Corps_of_Vatican_City_State "Gendarmerie Corps of Vatican City State") and the [Carabinieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carabinieri "Carabinieri"), paraded through St. Peter's Square and took up formation beneath the central [loggia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loggia "Loggia") of St. Peter's Basilica. From there, Cardinal Protodeacon [Dominique Mamberti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Mamberti "Dominique Mamberti") announced the election of Prevost[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Wooden-2025-162) and that he had taken the papal name _Leo XIV_.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Associated_Press-2025-163)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-164)

Leo XIV stepped onto the balcony shortly after the official announcement of his election, spoke to the crowd in St. Peter's Square and the world in Italian (while also briefly speaking in [Peruvian Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Spanish "Peruvian Spanish") to acknowledge the [Diocese of Chiclayo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Chiclayo "Roman Catholic Diocese of Chiclayo"), where he previously served as Bishop), expressed gratitude for Francis's legacy,[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-165) then delivered the _[Urbi et Orbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbi\_et\_Orbi "Urbi et Orbi")_ blessing.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Wooden-2025-162) He was accompanied by Ravelli, Marco Agostini, and Jean-Jacques Didier Bouable, who led the group as [cross-bearer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucifer "Crucifer"). The three were from the [Office for the Liturgical Celebrations of the Supreme Pontiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_for_the_Liturgical_Celebrations_of_the_Supreme_Pontiff "Office for the Liturgical Celebrations of the Supreme Pontiff").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Immediately after the appearance of white smoke, 40,000 were present in St. Peter's Square;[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-166) according to Italian law enforcement, by the time of the _[habemus papam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habemus\_papam "Habemus papam")_ announcement, there were up to 150,000 in the square.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-167)

Post-conclave events
--------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Post-conclave events")]

The Holy See Press Office announced the schedule of activities and liturgical celebrations following the election of Pope Leo XIV.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-168) He celebrated his first Mass as pope with the [College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals") in the Sistine Chapel at 11:00 am on 9 May 2025, the day after his election.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-169) On 10 May 2025, he met the College of Cardinals in the Synod Hall.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-170) In the morning of 11 May, he celebrated a private Mass at the [Vatican Grottoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Grottoes "Vatican Grottoes"),[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-171) paying homage to his predecessors, before delivering his first _[Regina caeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina\_caeli "Regina caeli")_ address from the central loggia of [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-172) After the address, Leo broke the seals to the [papal apartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_apartments "Papal apartments") of the [Apostolic Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Palace "Apostolic Palace"), accompanied by Parolin and Farrell.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-173)

Pope Leo XIV celebrated his [inauguration Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV") on 18 May 2025 at [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square").[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-174)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Vatican-Inauguration-2025-175) He took canonical possession of the three other major basilicas on 20 May ([Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_Saint_Paul_Outside_the_Walls "Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls")) and 25 May ([Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbasilica_of_Saint_John_Lateran "Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran") and [Basilica of St. Mary Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_Maggiore "Santa Maria Maggiore")).[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-176) He had his first general audience on 21 May. On 24 May, he met the Roman Curia and the Vatican City State employees. On 31 May, he conferred his first presbyteral ordination as bishop of Rome to the priests of the [Diocese of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_Rome "Diocese of Rome").[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-177)
